usageNotes: Immediately kills all processes in the container without a graceful shutdown — equivalent to pulling the power cord. Use only when the container is hung and unresponsive to a shutdown request, or when speed is more important than data integrity. Returns a task UPID; poll the task status to confirm the container reaches the 'stopped' state. Caller must hold VM.PowerMgmt on /vms/{vmid}.
destructiveReason: All processes in the container are killed instantly with no opportunity to flush buffers or run shutdown hooks, which can corrupt open files and databases.

examples.summary: Force-stop an unresponsive LXC container (vmid 201) on node pve1, aborting any pending vzshutdown task first

tips: Prefer post_nodes_node_lxc_vmid_status_shutdown for a clean stop; use this only when shutdown is stuck or unresponsive.
Set overrule-shutdown: true when a vzshutdown task is already queued — otherwise the stop may be blocked.
skiplock: true requires root and should be reserved for recovery scenarios where an administrative lock is orphaned.
